new_note: *The imperfect branches shall be broken off, their fruit unprofitable, not ripe to eat, yes, meet for nothing.* (Wisdom of Solomon 4:5). *And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.* (Matthew 21:19). Wisdom is describing branches that flourish for a season, bear nothing worth eating, and are broken off. The fig tree the King met on the road the morning after he cleansed the Temple was all leaves and no fruit, and he spoke its end on the spot. The tree was not the people of Yashar'el (Israel); it was the leadership standing in that Temple with every show of foliage and nothing to feed anyone, the same men he answers with seven woes in Matthew 23 before the week is out. The test he had already given his disciples was fruit, not leaves (Matthew 7:16), and Solomon had written the same verdict long before.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 4:5 — *The imperfect branches shall be broken off, their fruit unprofitable.* The fig tree with leaves and no fruit (Matthew 21:19) is the leadership, not the people; the branch that bears nothing is broken off.

new_note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:1). *Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 10:32). Wisdom looks to the day when the righteous man, whose labours his afflicters counted as nothing, stands in front of them in great boldness. The King gives his disciples the way into that day: confess him before men now, and he will confess them before the Father then. The confession is made in the face of the same people doing the afflicting, and the boldness Solomon saw is the boldness of the one being named by the Son in front of the Father while those who despised him look on.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 — *the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him.* The one who confesses the King before his afflicters (Matthew 10:32) is the one who stands in boldness before them on that day.

new_note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:1). *Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him.* (Matthew 12:14). The council that went out to plan his destruction was the system rendering its verdict on the righteous man. It had started by faulting his disciples, moved to calling him a drunkard and a friend of sinners, and now it was planning his death. Wisdom had already written the end of that story: the one the system condemned stands in great boldness before the faces of those who condemned him. The third day was the first installment of that standing, and the day of judgment is the rest of it, when the verdict rendered in this age is reversed in front of the men who rendered it.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 — *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him.* The council to destroy him (Matthew 12:14) is the verdict this age renders; the day of judgment reverses it in front of them.

new_note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:1). *From that time forth began Yahusha (Jesus) to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.* (Matthew 16:21). Here the King lays out both halves at once: he will suffer many things from the elders and chief priests and scribes, be killed, and be raised the third day. Solomon saw the second half from far off, the righteous man standing in boldness before the very men who afflicted him and made no account of his labours. The third day is where that standing begins, and the King finishes the thought a few verses later, when the Son of Adam comes in the glory of his Father to reward every man according to his works (Matthew 16:27). The vindication does not make him righteous; it shows in public what was true all along.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 — *stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* Killed and raised the third day (Matthew 16:21) is where the righteous man's standing before his afflicters begins.

new_note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:1). *And he saith unto them, Ye shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father.* (Matthew 20:23). The sons of Zebedee asked for the seats; the King promised them the cup. They would drink what he drank and be baptized with what he was baptized with, and the seats would be the Father's to assign. Wisdom puts the order the same way: the righteous man's labours are made no account of first, and the standing in great boldness comes after. The cup is the afflicting; the boldness before the afflicters is what follows it, and who sits where on that day is in the Father's hand, not seized along the road.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 — *the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him.* The cup the sons of Zebedee will drink (Matthew 20:23) comes first; the standing in boldness before the afflicters comes after.

new_note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:1). *Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels:* (Matthew 25:41). Wisdom and the King are describing the same day from two sides. On that day the righteous stand in great boldness, and the next verse in Wisdom has their afflicters troubled with terrible fear and amazed at a salvation they never looked for, which is exactly the astonishment of those on the left hand asking when they ever saw him hungry or thirsty (Matthew 25:44). Notice what the King says about the fire: it was prepared for the devil and his angels, the fallen ones Jude and Peter say are kept in chains for judgment (Jude 6; 2 Peter 2:4), and John sees the devil himself cast into that lake of fire (Revelation 20:10). The goats are sent toward a place that was not made for them. They are the unfruitful among the gathered, sifted before the reign, not the nations being judged for entry.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 — *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him.* The day the righteous stand in boldness is the day of Matthew 25:41; the fire was prepared for the devil and his angels, and the goats are the unfruitful among the gathered.

new_note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:1). *Ought not Messiah (Christ) to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory?* (Luke 24:26). On the road to Emmaus the King asks the two disciples whether the Messiah (Christ) ought not to have suffered these things and then enter his glory. Wisdom had already written the glory half: the righteous man, condemned in chapter 2 to a shameful death, now standing in great boldness before the faces of the men who did it. Suffering first, then the standing, is the shape he then shows them in Moses and all the prophets, and the Hebrew library had the same shape in Solomon's hand long before Luke wrote it down.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 — *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him.* The glory the Messiah (Christ) enters after suffering (Luke 24:26) is this standing in boldness before those who afflicted him.

new_note: *We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour:* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:4). *Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him.* (Matthew 12:14). The men who held a council to destroy him accounted his life madness; before long they will say he casts out devils by Beelzebub. Wisdom puts their own confession in their mouths at the judgment: we fools, we accounted his life madness and his end without honour. The council of Matthew 12:14 is the first step of that story, and the verse that follows in Wisdom is its last, when they see him numbered among the children of Yahuah (God). The same reversal waits for everyone the system counts a fool for walking in his commandments now.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:4 — *We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour.* The council to destroy him (Matthew 12:14) is the judgment of fools that the day of judgment turns into their own confession.

new_note: *How is he numbered among the children of Yahuah (God), and his lot is among the saints!* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:5). *Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world:* (Matthew 25:34). At the judgment his afflicters discover that the man they despised is numbered among the children of Yahuah (God) and has his lot among the saints. The King says where that lot came from: a kingdom prepared for the blessed from the foundation of the world. It was not assigned on the day; it was prepared before there was a world, and the day only reveals whose it was. Names were written in the Lamb's book from the foundation of the world (Revelation 13:8), and on that day the sheep hear the Shepherd say come, because they were his before they ever heard him.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:5 — *How is he numbered among the children of Yahuah (God), and his lot is among the saints.* The lot among the saints is the kingdom prepared from the foundation of the world (Matthew 25:34), revealed on the day, not assigned on it.

new_note: *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:8). *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess.* (Matthew 23:25). The pride and the riches were real; so was the vaunting. What Wisdom records is their worth on the day, which is nothing. The cup the King points at in the Temple court is the same lesson in a dish: clean on the outside where men can see it, extortion and excess on the inside where only the judgment will look. What has pride profited us is the question the inside of that cup will have to answer when the day of the righteous turns it over.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:8 — *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us.* The inside of the cup full of extortion and excess (Matthew 23:25) is what the day exposes, and pride will have profited nothing.

new_note: *But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with Yahuah (God), and the care of them is with the Most High.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:15). *Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?* (Matthew 6:26). The care of the righteous is with the Most High. That is the ground the King stands on when he tells his disciples to look at the birds: they neither sow nor reap nor fill barns, and the heavenly Father feeds them, and you are worth more than they. Taking no anxious thought is not a technique; it is what follows when you know whose care you are already in. Solomon named the care, and the King named the birds so his hearers could see it with their eyes.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:15 — *the care of them is with the Most High.* The Father who feeds the birds (Matthew 6:26) is the Most High whose care the righteous are already in.

new_note: *But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with Yahuah (God), and the care of them is with the Most High.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:15). *And he saith unto them, Ye shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father.* (Matthew 20:23). The righteous live for evermore and their reward is with Yahuah (God). It is kept in his hand, which is what the King tells the sons of Zebedee when they ask for the seats: to sit at his right hand and his left is not his to give, it is given to those for whom it is prepared of his Father. The reward is real and it is the Father's to give. It is not seized by flesh and it is not handed out regardless of the walk; it is held for the righteous by the one who sees their labours when no one else does.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:15 — *their reward also is with Yahuah (God).* The seats that are the Father's to give (Matthew 20:23) are the reward kept with Yahuah (God) for the righteous.

new_note: *But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with Yahuah (God), and the care of them is with the Most High.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:15). *And as they went to tell his disciples, behold, Yahusha (Jesus) met them, saying, All hail. And they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him.* (Matthew 28:9). The righteous live for evermore. The women at the tomb found out what that looks like: they held him by the feet. He had a body they could grip, flesh and bones he would show the disciples that evening (Luke 24:39), and that risen body is the firstfruits of what Wisdom promises the righteous. The righteous dead are not disembodied souls already in heaven; they are asleep, their reward kept with Yahuah (God), waiting for the day the one who rose first raises them (1 Thessalonians 4:16). The care of them is with the Most High the whole time they wait.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:15 — *But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with Yahuah (God).* The risen body the women held by the feet (Matthew 28:9) is the firstfruits of the righteous living for evermore.

new_note: *Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God): for with his right hand shall he cover them, and with his arm shall he protect them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:16). *But seek ye first the kingdom of Elohim (God), and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.* (Matthew 6:33). The kingdom and the crown come from the hand of Yahuah (God), and his right hand covers those who receive them. The King tells his disciples to seek that kingdom first and let the rest be added. Food and clothing are the small things the covering hand already holds for the one who is reaching for the kingdom itself; the same arm that protects the righteous in Wisdom is the one the King promises will add all these things.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:16 — *Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God).* Seek the kingdom first (Matthew 6:33); the kingdom and the crown come from the Father's hand, and all the rest is added.

new_note: *Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God): for with his right hand shall he cover them, and with his arm shall he protect them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:16). *And he saith unto him, Friend, how camest thou in hither not having a wedding garment? And he was speechless.* (Matthew 22:12). The guest came in without a wedding garment and had nothing to say. Wisdom shows what the garment was for: those who receive a glorious kingdom and a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God) receive them clothed. The fine linen of the bride is the righteousness of saints (Revelation 19:8), granted to her and then worn, and the man at the feast had neither put it on nor walked in it. The crown is given from the Father's hand to those who came dressed for the feast; the one who came in his own clothes receives the silence and the door.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:16 — *Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God).* The man without a wedding garment (Matthew 22:12) has no crown to receive; the kingdom and the crown go to those clothed for the feast.

new_note: *Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God): for with his right hand shall he cover them, and with his arm shall he protect them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:16). *And as they went to tell his disciples, behold, Yahusha (Jesus) met them, saying, All hail. And they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him.* (Matthew 28:9). The women held the risen King by the feet and worshipped him. He is the first of the righteous to receive the glorious kingdom from the Father's hand, and the crown Wisdom speaks of is the one Paul expects at his appearing (2 Timothy 4:8) and the one the King promises to the faithful unto death (Revelation 2:10). The right hand that covers the righteous is the hand he will name a few verses later when he says all power is given unto him in heaven and in earth (Matthew 28:18). What the women touched that morning was the first of the resurrected righteous, crowned.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:16 — *a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God): for with his right hand shall he cover them.* The risen King the women worshipped (Matthew 28:9) is the first of the righteous to receive the kingdom and the crown from the Father's hand.

new_note: *Because, being ministers of his kingdom, you have not judged aright, nor kept the law, nor walked after the counsel of Yahuah (God);* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:4). *But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in.* (Matthew 23:13). Wisdom addresses men who hold office as ministers of his kingdom and have not judged aright, nor kept the law, nor walked after his counsel. The King addresses the same office in the Temple court: men who hold the keys of the kingdom of heaven, do not go in themselves, and shut the door on those who are entering. The test is the one John gives plainly, that he who says he knows him and keeps not his commandments is a liar (1 John 2:4), and a ministry that sets aside the law it was given to keep fails it in whatever century it stands. The woe is on the office and the system; the men in it had the lie handed to them, and the people under them are the ones being shut out.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 6:4 — *being ministers of his kingdom, you have not judged aright, nor kept the law.* Ministers who have not kept the law are the ones who shut up the kingdom against men (Matthew 23:13).

new_note: *Horribly and speedily shall he come upon you: for a sharp judgment shall be to them that be in high places.* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:5). *Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.* (Matthew 11:21). A sharp judgment belongs to those in high places. Chorazin and Bethsaida were set in a high place: the mighty works were done in their streets, and they did not repent. Tyre and Sidon, cities the prophets thundered against, would have been in sackcloth long ago if they had seen the same works. The more that is shown to a city or a man, the sharper the reckoning, and Solomon had written that rule before the King applied it to the towns he had been healing in.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 6:5 — *a sharp judgment shall be to them that be in high places.* Chorazin and Bethsaida (Matthew 11:21) saw the mighty works and did not repent; the more shown, the sharper the judgment.

new_note: *For mercy will soon pardon the meanest: but mighty men shall be mightily tormented.* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:6). *But I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment, than for you.* (Matthew 11:22). Mercy soon pardons the lowly; the mighty are mightily tormented. The King says it over the towns that saw his works: more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment than for you. The judgment is real and it has degrees. Those who were shown little answer for little; those who were shown the kingdom working in their own streets answer for that. It is not one flat torment for everyone and it is not nothing; it is weighed.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 6:6 — *mercy will soon pardon the meanest: but mighty men shall be mightily tormented.* More tolerable for Tyre and Sidon (Matthew 11:22): the judgment is real and weighed by what each was shown.

new_note: *But a sore trial shall come upon the mighty.* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:8). *And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.* (Matthew 11:23). A sore trial comes upon the mighty. Capernaum was mighty in the one way that counts in this chapter: it was exalted unto heaven, the King's own city where he lived and healed and taught. The sore trial for a city like that is to be brought down to hell, the grave, the place of the dead, lower than Sodom. The hell here is the pit the city goes down into, not the endless fire the pulpit reads into the word. Sodom would have stood if it had seen what Capernaum saw.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 6:8 — *But a sore trial shall come upon the mighty.* Capernaum, exalted unto heaven and brought down to the grave (Matthew 11:23), is the mighty under the sore trial.

new_note: *Wisdom is glorious, and never fadeth away: yes, she is easily seen of them that love her, and found of such as seek her.* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:12). *Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:* (Matthew 7:7). Wisdom is found of such as seek her. The King's three verbs, ask, seek, knock, carry the same promise: it will be given, you will find, it will be opened. Solomon adds that she is easily seen of them that love her, which means the seeking is not a long climb but a turning toward what is already in view. The Father gives the good gift to those who ask, and Luke names the gift as the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) (Luke 11:13), which is the spirit of wisdom Solomon himself prayed for.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 6:12 — *she is easily seen of them that love her, and found of such as seek her.* Seek and ye shall find (Matthew 7:7) is the promise Solomon wrote about wisdom first.

new_note: *She preventeth them that desire her, in making herself first known to them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:13). *Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:* (Matthew 7:7). Preventeth in the old sense means goes before. Wisdom does not wait to be caught; she goes out ahead of those who desire her and makes herself known first. That is what the King's ask, seek, knock rests on: the disciple is not climbing up to a Father who has to be found, he is knocking on a door the Father is already standing behind. The asking is answered, the seeking finds, the knocking opens, because the one being sought came out to meet the seeker before the seeker set out.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 6:13 — *She preventeth them that desire her, in making herself first known to them.* Wisdom goes before those who desire her; the Father answers ask, seek, knock (Matthew 7:7) because he came out to meet the seeker first.

new_note: *And love is the keeping of her laws; and the giving heed to her laws is the assurance of incorruption;* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:18). *On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.* (Matthew 22:40). Love is the keeping of her laws. The King hangs all the law and the prophets on two commandments, love of Yahuah (God) and love of neighbour, and the pulpit has used that sentence for centuries to say love replaced the law. Solomon says the opposite: love is what keeping the law looks like, and heed to her laws is the assurance of incorruption. John says it the same way, that this is the love of Elohim (God), that we keep his commandments (1 John 5:3). The two commandments are not a shorter list; they are the heart the whole Torah hangs from, the heart Ezekiel promised would be new so the statutes could be walked (Ezekiel 36:27).
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 6:18 — *love is the keeping of her laws; and the giving heed to her laws is the assurance of incorruption.* The two commandments all the law hangs on (Matthew 22:40) do not replace the law; love is the keeping of it.

new_note: *As for wisdom, what she is, and how she came up, I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you: but will seek her out from the beginning of her nativity, and bring the knowledge of her into light, and will not pass over the truth.* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:22). *That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world.* (Matthew 13:35). Solomon promises to tell what wisdom is and how she came up, to hide no mysteries, to trace her from the beginning of her nativity and bring the knowledge of her into light. The King opens his mouth in parables to utter things kept secret from the foundation of the world. Both are teachers who refuse to pass over the truth; both are bringing into the light what had been hidden, and the parables, which the crowd heard as stories, were that light being given to the disciples who asked what they meant.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 6:22 — *I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you.* Things kept secret from the foundation of the world uttered in parables (Matthew 13:35) is the same refusal to hide mysteries.

new_note: *Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came to me.* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:7). *At that time Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Yahuah (Lord) of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.* (Matthew 11:25). Solomon prayed, and understanding was given him; he called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came. The King thanks the Father that these things were hidden from the wise and prudent and revealed unto babes. The two agree on where understanding comes from: it is given. Solomon asked and it was given him; the babes had nothing in hand and it was revealed to them; the wise and prudent, sure they already had it, were passed over.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 7:7 — *I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came to me.* Understanding is given to the one who prays; the Father reveals to babes what the wise cannot reach (Matthew 11:25).

new_note: *I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:8). *Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchant man, seeking goodly pearls:* (Matthew 13:45). A king with a sceptre and a throne in hand says he preferred wisdom before both of them and counted riches nothing beside her. The merchant in the parable does the same arithmetic over one pearl: he sells all he has to get it. The kingdom of heaven is worth that reckoning, and the one who makes it is not throwing away sceptres and riches so much as seeing, as Solomon saw, that they were never worth what wisdom is. The pearl is found by someone already seeking goodly pearls; the finding is the moment everything else is weighed and comes up light.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 7:8 — *I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.* The merchant who sells all for one pearl (Matthew 13:45) is doing Solomon's arithmetic: sceptres and riches are nothing beside wisdom.
flag: Old note identified the buyer of the pearl as the Father or Son who pays all to obtain, citing an internal file (short.md). I could not verify that reading in the skill, so the rebuilt note keeps the plain comparison (king prefers wisdom / merchant sells all) and does not name who the buyer is. Author may want the buyer identification restored if it is settled teaching.

new_note: *For she is a treasure to men that never fails: which they that use become the friends of Yahuah (God), being commended for the gifts that come from learning.* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:14). *Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man hath found, he hideth, and for joy thereof goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field.* (Matthew 13:44). Wisdom is a treasure to men that never fails, and those who use her become the friends of Yahuah (God). The King says the kingdom of heaven is like treasure hid in a field, found by a man who hides it again, sells all he has for joy, and buys the field. Solomon's treasure and the King's treasure are the same kind: worth everything a man owns, and the man who finds it knows it. The one who learns wisdom is commended for her gifts; the one who buys the field has the treasure and the friendship of the one who hid it there.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 7:14 — *she is a treasure to men that never fails: which they that use become the friends of Yahuah (God).* The treasure hid in a field worth selling all for (Matthew 13:44) is the treasure that never fails and makes friends of Yahuah (God).
flag: Old note's buyer reading (Father or Son as the one who finds and pays all) rested on an internal reference I could not confirm in the skill; the rebuilt note leaves the buyer unnamed and keeps the treasure comparison.

new_note: *For she is the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:25). *Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;* (Hebrews 1:3). A pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: Wisdom describes something that comes out of the glory without lessening it. Hebrews puts a person where Wisdom put a picture. The Son is the brightness of his glory and the express image of his person, the way light shining is of the light and yet is not the lamp. He proceeds from the Father as brightness proceeds from light, the Formed shining out from the Formless: Elohim (God) who has a Father, the one who upholds all things by the word of his power and then sat down at the right hand of the one he came from.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 7:25 — *a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.* What flows out from the glory without lessening it is a person in Hebrews 1:3, the brightness of his glory.

new_note: *For she is the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:25). *Who, being in the form of Elohim (God), thought it not robbery to be equal with Elohim (God):* (Philippians 2:6). The Hebrew library saw Wisdom as the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty. Brought forth from him, carrying his glory, and not a second god standing beside him. Paul describes the same one as being in the form of Elohim (God) and counting it no robbery to be equal with Elohim (God), and then in the next breath emptying himself. What flows from the glory is of the glory, so the equality is no theft; and what flows has a source, so he has a Father and takes the lower place freely. The Formed is not a rival to the Formless; he is what the Formless breathed out.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 7:25 — *the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.* The breath of the power flowing from the glory is the one in the form of Elohim (God) (Philippians 2:6), brought forth, not a rival.

new_note: *O Yahuah (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (God) of mercy, who have made all things with your word,* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:1). *But straightway Yahusha (Jesus) spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.* (Matthew 14:27). Solomon prays to the Elohim (God) of his fathers who made all things with his word. John says the same of the Word: all things were made by him, and without him was not any thing made that was made (John 1:3). In the fourth watch the disciples see a figure walking on the sea and cry out, and he answers with the name the Formed one spoke from the bush: it is I, be not afraid. The one walking on the water is the Word the sea was made with, come in flesh and standing on his own handiwork. The Father made all things with his word; here the word is walking toward the boat.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 9:1 — *who have made all things with your word.* The Word all things were made with walks on the sea and says it is I (Matthew 14:27).

new_note: *O Yahuah (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (God) of mercy, who have made all things with your word,* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:1). *They say unto him, Cæsar’s. Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Cæsar the things which are Cæsar’s; and unto Elohim (God) the things that are Elohim's (God’s).* (Matthew 22:21). Caesar's face on the coin makes the coin Caesar's. Solomon's prayer tells you what makes everything else the Father's: he made all things with his word, and the next verse adds that he ordained man through his wisdom to rule over what was made. So when the King says render unto Elohim (God) the things that are Elohim's (God's), the things in question are all things, man first, because man carries the Maker's image the way the denarius carries Caesar's. The Word the Father made all things with is the one standing in the court holding the coin and asking whose image is on it.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 9:1 — *who have made all things with your word.* Render unto Elohim (God) the things that are his (Matthew 22:21): all things, since he made them all with his word.

new_note: *Of whose wickedness even to this day the waste land that smoketh is a testimony, and plants bearing fruit that never come to ripeness: and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul.* (Wisdom of Solomon 10:7). *But I say unto you, That it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee.* (Matthew 11:24). The waste land still smoking, the fruit that never ripens, the pillar of salt standing as a monument of an unbelieving soul: Sodom was still preaching in Solomon's day. The King uses that monument as the floor. If the works done in Capernaum had been done in Sodom, Sodom would still be standing, and so it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment than for the town that saw the kingdom at work in its own streets and did not turn. The smoking land is the witness against the unbelieving soul; the city with the mighty works has a sharper witness against it.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 10:7 — *a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul.* Sodom, the standing monument of unbelief, is the floor the King measures Capernaum against (Matthew 11:24).

new_note: *And left him not in bonds, till she brought him the sceptre of the kingdom, and power against those that oppressed him: as for them that had accused him, she shewed them to be liars, and gave him perpetual glory.* (Wisdom of Solomon 10:14). *He made him lord of his house, and ruler of all his substance:* (Psalm 105:21). Joseph was sold, went down into the pit, and was not left in bonds. Wisdom says she brought him the sceptre of the kingdom and power against those that oppressed him, showed his accusers to be liars, and gave him perpetual glory. The psalm tells it as history: Pharaoh made him lord of his house and ruler of all he had, and the next verse adds that he bound Pharaoh's princes at his pleasure and taught his senators wisdom (Psalm 105:22). The bound man binds the princes; the man accused as a liar is the one who ends up teaching the court. Wisdom went down into the pit with him and came up with him to the throne.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 10:14 — *left him not in bonds, till she brought him the sceptre of the kingdom.* Joseph, not left in bonds but made lord of Pharaoh's house (Psalm 105:21), is the sold man raised to the sceptre.

new_note: *But executing your judgments upon them by little and little, you gavest them place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.* (Wisdom of Solomon 12:10). *And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of Adam, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.* (Matthew 12:32). Yahuah (God) executed his judgments on the Canaanites little by little and gave them place of repentance, knowing all the while that their malice was bred in them and their cogitation would never be changed; the next verse calls them a cursed seed from the beginning. The King speaks of a sin that will not be forgiven in this world or the one to come, the word spoken against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) by men who had just watched the Spirit cast out devils and called it Beelzebub. Both passages describe a disposition that does not change: room to repent is given, and the heart that was never going to turn uses the room to harden. He said of such hearers that they believe not because they are not of his sheep (John 10:26).
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 12:10 — *their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.* The cogitation that would never be changed is the heart behind the word against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) that is not forgiven (Matthew 12:32).

new_note: *But by such works have you taught your people that the just man should be merciful, and have made your children to be of a good hope that you give repentance for sins.* (Wisdom of Solomon 12:19). *But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;* (Matthew 5:44). Solomon says the Father's dealings with Yashar'el's (Israel's) enemies were themselves the lesson: by such works he taught his people that the just man should be merciful, and gave his children good hope that he gives repentance for sins. The King teaches the same lesson from the same source. Love your enemies, bless those who curse you, pray for those who persecute you, and the reason follows in the next verse: so that you may be children of your Father, who does exactly that. The mercy the children show is learned from watching the Father show it.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 12:19 — *by such works have you taught your people that the just man should be merciful.* Love your enemies (Matthew 5:44) is the lesson the Father taught by his own mercy on enemies.

new_note: *For if you did punish the enemies of your children, and the condemned to death, with such deliberation, giving them time and place, by which they might be delivered from their malice:* (Wisdom of Solomon 12:20). *That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.* (Matthew 5:45). Even the enemies of his children, even those already condemned to death, he punished with deliberation, giving them time and place to be delivered from their malice. The King points at the sky for the same pattern: the Father makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good and sends rain on the just and on the unjust. The wicked are still being given daylight and harvest, which is time and place to turn. Children who love their enemies in this age are copying a Father who has been doing it since before the land was given.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 12:20 — *giving them time and place, by which they might be delivered from their malice.* Sun on the evil and rain on the unjust (Matthew 5:45) is the time and place the Father gives enemies to turn.

new_note: *But your providence, O Father, governeth it: for you have made a way in the sea, and a safe path in the waves;* (Wisdom of Solomon 14:3). *And he saith unto them, Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.* (Matthew 8:26). The Father's providence governs the sea; he has made a way in it and a safe path in the waves. The Father governs the sea through his Word, the one who made the way in it, and on the lake of Galilee that one was asleep in the stern of a fishing boat while the disciples thought they were dying. He woke, rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm. The voice Solomon credits with governing the waters was in the boat in flesh, and the rebuke that calmed the water was the same governance Wisdom had named, exercised from a wet deck by the one who had made the way in the sea in the first place.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 14:3 — *your providence, O Father, governeth it: for you have made a way in the sea.* The one who rebuked the winds and the sea (Matthew 8:26) is the one whose providence governs it.

new_note: *But your providence, O Father, governeth it: for you have made a way in the sea, and a safe path in the waves;* (Wisdom of Solomon 14:3). *And in the fourth watch of the night Yahusha (Jesus) went unto them, walking on the sea.* (Matthew 14:25). The Father has made a way in the sea and a safe path in the waves; the psalmist says the same, that his way is in the sea and his path in the great waters (Psalm 77:19). In the fourth watch the King walks that way, on the water, toward a boat full of men being tossed by it. The Formed one walks the path the Father's providence made, and when Peter steps out and sinks, the hand that catches him (Matthew 14:31) is the safe path in the waves Solomon prayed about. The way in the sea was never a figure of speech; a man walked it.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 14:3 — *you have made a way in the sea, and a safe path in the waves.* The King walking on the sea in the fourth watch (Matthew 14:25) is walking the way the Father made in the sea.

new_note: *Shewing that you can save from all danger: yes, though a man went to sea without art.* (Wisdom of Solomon 14:4). *And he saith unto them, Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.* (Matthew 8:26). Solomon says the Father can save from all danger at sea, even a man who went out without the skill to be there. The disciples were fishermen, and the storm outdid their skill anyway; their cry was Lord, save us, we perish (Matthew 8:25). He answered by asking why they were fearful and then rebuking the wind and the water into a great calm. The saving Solomon prayed about was done in front of them, by the one in the boat, and the rebuke of their little faith is that they had the governor of the sea aboard and thought they were on their own.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 14:4 — *Shewing that you can save from all danger.* Lord, save us, we perish (Matthew 8:25) is answered by the one who can save from all danger at sea (Matthew 8:26).

new_note: *For you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:13). *He said unto them, Give place: for the maid is not dead, but sleepeth. And they laughed him to scorn.* (Matthew 9:24). Power of life and death belongs to Yahuah (God): he leads to the gates of hell, the grave, and brings up again. In the ruler's house the King looked at a dead girl and said she was not dead but sleeping, and the mourners laughed at him. Then he took her by the hand and she arose. The one who brings up again from the gates of the grave was standing in the room in flesh, and death in his presence is sleep because he is the one who wakes it. The righteous dead are asleep the same way, and the hand that took the girl's hand is the one that will bring them up.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 — *you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* The maid not dead but sleeping (Matthew 9:24) is raised by the one who leads to the grave and brings up again.
